evidence.summary: Ran kernel.run on all 63488 finite FP16 values (exhaustive legal domain) on GPU; compared against FP64 rho = sqrt(1+x^2)-1 on exact stored values. 0 violations of abs(err) <= 1e-8 + 1e-5*|rho|; worst margin err-tol = -1e-8. Max abs err 3.05e-4 occurs at large x where tolerance is 0.655, comfortably satisfied; near-zero inputs satisfy the 1e-8 absolute floor.

rationale: The kernel computes x*x/(sqrt(1+x*x)+1) in FP32, algebraically equal to sqrt(1+x*x)-1, so FP32 intermediate rounding is the only error source, likely well within 1e-8+1e-5*|rho|. Exhaustively testing every finite FP16 value in FP64 reference will decide.

scope_evidence.summary: Contract: EVERY finite FP16 value is legal including signed zeros, subnormals and ±65504, and every output element must satisfy abs(actual[i]-rho(x[i])) <= 1e-8 + 1e-5*abs(rho(x[i])); correctness is one verdict for the whole legal domain.

scope_rationale: The contract requires the tolerance bound on every finite FP16 input (all 65536 values, incl. subnormals and ±65504), so any elementwise violation on an exhaustively enumerated legal input is a contract violation.
statement: For every legal finite FP16 input value (all 65536 bit patterns including signed zeros, subnormals, ±65504), the Triton kernel's FP32 output satisfies abs(actual - rho_fp64(x)) <= 1e-8 + 1e-5*abs(rho_fp64(x)).
